author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Saffie Osborne made British horse-racing history Saturday by riding Highwayman to victory in the St Leger Stakes at Doncaster. She became the first female jockey to win one of the five Classics of British flat racing, reaching the milestone on the 250th anniversary of the world’s oldest Classic.

Highwayman entered at odds of 11-1 and finished two-and-a-half lengths ahead of Enceladus, giving trainer Joseph O’Brien a one-two result. Amelia Earhart placed third at 22-1 before a crowd of about 30,000. The St Leger, first run in 1776, is the final British Classic of the season.

Osborne had not expected to ride in the race a week earlier, making the late opportunity and victory especially striking. Women had won many prominent races in Britain before Saturday, but none of the Classics: the 1,000 Guineas, 2,000 Guineas, Oaks, Derby and St Leger. Her win breaks that barrier in the oldest of the five.
dek: Osborne rode 11-1 Highwayman to victory in the St Leger Stakes on the race’s 250th anniversary.
headline: Saffie Osborne becomes first female jockey to win a British Classic
